country_overview: Morocco's currency is the Moroccan dirham (MAD). Bank Al-Maghrib administers a gradual exchange-rate reform in which the dirham fluctuates within a ±5% band around a central rate based on a currency basket composed of the euro (60%) and the US dollar (40%) — a monetary-regime fact kept analytically separate from exchange-control law. Cross-border FX operations remain under the regulated foreign-exchange framework administered by the Office des Changes. The Instruction Générale des Opérations de Change 2026 (IGOC 2026) entered into force on 1 January 2026 and is the current controlling general instruction. Border reporting of foreign means/instruments under Art. 37 (>= MAD 100,000) is distinct from the physical-MAD banknote carriage rule under Art. 42 (<= MAD 2,000). Resident, non-resident, account-eligibility, travel-allowance and business operations are category- and article-specific under IGOC 2026; absence of a located restriction is not evidence that none exists.

summary.traveler: At entry, under IGOC 2026 Art. 37, effects of commerce, means of payment and financial instruments are subject to Customs declaration when their value is equal to or greater than MAD 100,000 (>=); below that amount declaration is optional. Presentation of the import declaration remains mandatory to justify origin for certain later operations (eligible FX/convertible-dirham account funding, re-export of foreign currency, or qualifying export-proceeds cases), regardless of amount. Separately, under Art. 42, import and export of Moroccan dirham banknotes are prohibited in principle, except travellers may carry banknotes not exceeding MAD 2,000 (<=). These are two distinct regimes.
summary.business: IGOC 2026 provides a regulated, category-specific framework. Goods-export proceeds must generally be repatriated within 150 days of Customs-declaration registration (Art. 89), with goods-exporter FX/convertible-dirham accounts under Art. 90. Service-export proceeds must generally be repatriated within 90 days of performance (Art. 97), with service-exporter accounts under Art. 98. Service imports (Arts 69–72) include transaction categories requiring prior Office des Changes agreement. Settlements run through authorised intermediary banks; this is not a claim that all cross-border business is unrestricted.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: IGOC 2026 Art. 36 permits resident and non-resident natural persons to import foreign-currency payment instruments and bearer negotiable instruments without a quantitative import ceiling. Art. 37 then requires Customs declaration at entry when effects of commerce, means of payment and bearer negotiable financial instruments have a value equal to or greater than MAD 100,000 (>=; égale ou supérieure) — not merely '>'. Below MAD 100,000, declaration is facultative. Office des Changes FAQ and Art. 37 further require presentation of the import declaration to justify origin for funding eligible FX/convertible-dirham accounts, re-export of the currencies, or where repatriated banknotes constitute export proceeds of goods/services — regardless of amount. The declaration is valid up to one month for residents and six months for non-residents and must be annotated by the bank for amounts collected. This is a declaration architecture, not an import ceiling, and is not Art. 42's physical-MAD banknote rule.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Outbound FX is residency- and source-specific under IGOC 2026 Art. 40. Resident natural persons may export payment instruments granted under the exchange regulations; foreign-banknote export must occur within 30 days of grant of the FX allocation, failing which the currency must be surrendered/re-sold, and departure requires the change slip and/or debit advice from an eligible FX/convertible-dirham account. Foreign non-residents and Moroccans residing abroad may export foreign-currency payment instruments previously imported, with foreign banknotes / bearer negotiable instruments requiring the relevant Customs declaration and inbound-import proof. Art. 40 also imposes an exit Customs declaration when covered effects / means of payment / bearer negotiable instruments equal or exceed MAD 100,000 (>=), kept separate from resident allocation rules and non-resident re-export provenance. Separately, Art. 41 provides a special MRE repurchase path: MRE may repurchase from banks/authorised exchange operators and export foreign currency previously repatriated and sold on the FX market during the previous 12 months, subject to the article's annual ceiling and documentation — not to be collapsed into ordinary non-resident re-export. Physical MAD banknotes remain under Art. 42 (<= MAD 2,000).
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: Two separate numeric architectures must not be collapsed. (1) Art. 37 / Art. 40: foreign means/instruments — mandatory Customs declaration when value is equal to or greater than MAD 100,000 (>=) at entry and at exit; below MAD 100,000 entry declaration is facultative; documentation may still be required regardless of amount for specified later operations. (2) Art. 42: physical Moroccan dirham banknotes — import/export prohibited in principle, with a traveller exception not exceeding MAD 2,000 (<=). The MAD 100,000 figure is a declaration trigger, not a carriage ceiling and not the MAD 2,000 dirham-banknote rule.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Under IGOC 2026 Art. 38, foreign-currency payment instruments imported by residents, regardless of amount, must generally be surrendered to banks, authorised currency-exchange operators or authorised sub-delegates within a period not exceeding 30 days from entry. Within that window, foreign residents and exporters of goods and/or services may credit qualifying foreign banknotes to eligible FX/convertible-dirham accounts (Arts 90, 98 and/or 228 as applicable). Foreign residents may also hold, without that banknote surrender clock, specified non-banknote instruments issued abroad (traveller's cheques, bank/postal cheques, letters of credit, payment cards and similar) where Art. 38 so provides. Separately, Art. 140 defines eligible personal-travel beneficiaries; Art. 141 sets the numeric allowance — base MAD 100,000 plus a supplement equal to 30% of prior-year income tax paid/withheld, total not exceeding MAD 500,000 per person per calendar year; Art. 142 governs payment modalities (banks, exchange operators, cards, agency paths). These rules do not establish a universal resident right to hold any foreign-currency product, nor a blanket prohibition on all resident FX holding.
rules.non_resident_rules: Under IGOC 2026 Art. 38, natural-person non-residents may exchange imported foreign currency for MAD or retain it and exchange it progressively according to their needs. For qualifying foreign-investment operations, non-residents may pay in foreign banknotes within six months of entry into eligible Art. 228 FX/convertible-dirham accounts. Do not collapse foreign residents (Art. 38 resident limb / account qualifications) with non-residents. Banks are authorised under Art. 228 to open FX and convertible-dirham accounts for: foreign natural persons (resident or non-resident); Moroccans residing abroad; foreign legal persons and their representations; industrial acceleration-zone companies; offshore financial-centre entities; diplomatic representations; and international organisations and their representations. Credits may include incoming foreign transfers, transfers from eligible FX/convertible-dirham accounts, and qualifying instruments; foreign-banknote deposits require the inbound declaration (generally within six months) or other specified proof. Debits cover qualifying transfers, FX-market sales and withdrawals under the article. Account eligibility is not unrestricted convertibility of every source of funds. Exporter accounts are separate (Arts 90 and 98).
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Business cross-border operations remain under IGOC 2026 via authorised intermediary banks. Goods exports: Art. 89 requires repatriation of the full export proceeds, generally within 150 days from registration of the Customs declaration (subject to article-specific exceptions); Art. 90 authorises goods-exporter FX/convertible-dirham accounts. Service exports: Art. 97 requires repatriation within 90 days from performance of the service; Art. 98 authorises service-exporter FX/convertible-dirham accounts. Service imports: Arts 69–72 define the regime; Art. 71 includes transaction categories requiring prior Office des Changes agreement (including certain parent-company cost allocations, guaranteed franchise entry fees/minimum royalties, and intermediary collection of funds for non-resident services). Do not summarise Morocco as 'all service imports freely payable'. Arts 90/98 exporter accounts are distinct from Art. 228 foreign-person/MRE/listed-entity accounts.
rules.exchange_controls: Morocco remains a regulated foreign-exchange jurisdiction administered by the Office des Changes. IGOC 2026 is the current general instruction (in force 1 January 2026) continuing gradual, controlled liberalisation while preserving external balances. Operative architecture is transaction- and category-specific (Arts 36–42 border/cash architecture; travel Arts 140–142; goods/services export Arts 89–90 and 97–98; service-import Arts 69–72; account Arts 90, 98, 228; authorised intermediaries) rather than a single universal prior-approval screen for every payment and rather than full liberalisation. The Bank Al-Maghrib ±5% fluctuation band around the EUR60/USD40 basket is a separate monetary-regime fact.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign-exchange conversion for the public is available through authorised intermediary banks and through Office des Changes-authorised currency-exchange operators and sub-delegates. The Instruction régissant l'activité de change de devises dated 15 June 2026 defines authorisation, operating, recording, declarative and AML-related requirements for the licensed manual-exchange sector (in force 15 June 2026). FX conversion is therefore a licensed multi-channel activity, not bank-only and not an unregulated free-for-all. That Instruction does not itself establish resident capital-account rights. Availability of a particular currency, rate or product remains subject to licence scope, documentary rules and commercial terms.
